subject.title: Externally-registered cron jobs auto-enable without user confirmation, inherit expensive default model, no usage circuit breaker

question: What default safety policy should OpenClaw apply to externally or declaratively registered cron jobs that can start recurring model calls?
rationale: The fix changes scheduler activation defaults, plugin/agent scheduling authority, model-cost policy, quota thresholds, and upgrade/doctor behavior, so automation should not choose the product/security contract alone.

options.title: Adopt a coordinated scheduler-safety policy
options.body: Require explicit activation or confirmation for external/declarative recurring jobs and add provenance, model-cost guardrails, update/doctor diffs, budget or circuit-breaking behavior, tests, and docs together.

options.title: Split and track slices separately
options.body: Keep this issue as the umbrella while landing #71712 provenance, #14376 reason-aware circuit breakers, and #42475 budget enforcement as separate canonical work with shared acceptance criteria.

options.title: Defer core default changes
options.body: Keep current enabled-by-default behavior, document the cost risk, and rely on explicit per-job model/disable settings instead of adding new core guardrails now.

recommendation.title: Adopt a coordinated scheduler-safety policy
recommendation.body: Require explicit activation or confirmation for external/declarative recurring jobs and add provenance, model-cost guardrails, update/doctor diffs, budget or circuit-breaking behavior, tests, and docs together.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal for the inherited-model and cron fallback behavior is recent cron model-selection work, and the decision spans product/security policy rather than a mechanical patch.
